prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1058; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss from insured. Insured reports vehicle struck while turning left at an intersection; other driver's vehicle was proceeding straight. Insured is not reporting injury at this time. Photos requested and assigned to field appraiser.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. Representation letter received requesting all communications be directed to their office. Claimant reports headache, dizziness, and light sensitivity following the collision and has been evaluated for a concussion. Medical authorization forms sent to counsel.

Entry 3: Reviewed police report. Responding officer notes the claimant's vehicle entered the intersection on a green signal and the insured's left turn was made against oncoming traffic. Fault assessment preliminarily leans toward the insured. Recorded statements from both drivers and one independent witness are pending.

Entry 4: Spoke with claimant's attorney regarding the concussion diagnosis. Counsel provided treating physician notes describing post-concussive symptoms and a recommended period of rest with follow-up imaging. Requested itemized medical bills and wage loss documentation. Reserve adjusted to reflect bodily injury exposure and referred to the bodily injury unit for review.

Entry 5: Received updated medical records from claimant's treating neurologist confirming ongoing concussion symptoms and a referral to a specialist. Counsel has requested a settlement conference once treatment milestones are documented. Supervisor notified of potential litigation risk. Next step: obtain independent medical review and confirm the insured's liability position before any offer is discussed.
